author: tvarohohlavy
body:
## Summary

`evidence.compare` only ever failed on a difference (`comparison_type` defaulted to `"exact"` and wasn't a declared config field), so it could not express *"a change is the expected, successful outcome"* — and it compared **every** shared artifact, including routing/neighbor tables whose uptime and timer columns drift every second and therefore always differ. The step could never pass for a flow that intentionally changes device state.

This surfaces the behavior as real, editable config fields on `evidence.compare`:

- **`comparison_type`** (`exact` | `changed` | `subset` | `superset` | `json_diff`) — `exact` fails on a difference (drift / no-change checks); **`changed` passes on one** (confirm an intended change took effect). Now a declared `Literal` field with clear option labels, so it appears in the step editor.
- **`artifact_name_pattern`** — a glob over artifact names (e.g. `*show running-config`), so volatile outputs (routing/neighbor tables) can be left out and only meaningful evidence is compared. An exact `artifact_name` still wins over the pattern.
- **`ignore_patterns`** — regexes whose matches are **masked in place** from both sides before a text comparison, so inline counters/timers/uptimes don't register as a difference *while the rest of the line — and any genuinely new lines — are kept*.

## Why masking, not line-dropping

Route/neighbor uptime counters are inline within otherwise-meaningful lines. Dropping whole matching lines would delete every route line (they all carry a timer), destroying the ability to detect a newly-announced prefix. `ignore_patterns` therefore does a substring `re.sub` (per-line, `^`/`$` anchored), normalizing the volatile columns while preserving real changes. A unit test pins exactly this.

## Tests

`tests/test_evidence_compare.py` covers:
- the `exact` ↔ `changed` inversion,
- timer masking that still surfaces a genuinely new prefix,
- invalid-pattern tolerance (skipped with a warning, never raised).

`ruff` / `ty` clean; full `test_core_handlers` + `test_sdk_contract` + new tests green (48 passed).

## Compatibility

`extra="allow"` is retained, so existing flow configs are unaffected. `comparison_type` was already read at runtime, so the new field only makes it visible/validated; `artifact_name_pattern` and `ignore_patterns` are additive and default to no-ops.

## Consumer

Used by the demo's *"Ops: Announce service prefix"* flow (`hegemony-demo-data`), which now confirms the running config actually changed instead of failing on the always-drifting routing table.

author: unpunnyfuns
body:
`RealisedToken<T>['$value']` was `unknown`; it is now typed per `$type` via a new exported `TokenValue<T>` mapped type, so a presenter holding a concrete `RealisedToken<T>` reads the right envelope without re-casting. The **top-level** shape is typed; sub-values stay `unknown` (a sub-value may be a primitive, a resolved alias string, or a nested composite), consistent with the existing envelope philosophy. A wrong-shape `$value` literal for a concrete `T` is now a compile error.

Part 1 of #1415 (the presenter-tier follow-ups); part 2 (the previewValue precedence fix) landed in #1432.

## What changed

- New `DimensionValue` envelope (`{ value, unit }`, DTCG 2025.10) and the `TokenValue<T>` mapped type covering every `TokenType` (color→ColorValue, gradient→GradientStop[], shadow→ShadowLayer|ShadowLayer[], typography→TypographyValue, border→BorderValue, transition→TransitionValue, strokeStyle→string|DashedStrokeStyleValue, fontFamily→string|string[], fontWeight→number|string, number→number, cubicBezier→number[], dimension/duration→string|number|DimensionValue).
- `RealisedToken<T>['$value']` retyped to `TokenValue<T>`.
- Dropped the now-redundant envelope casts in `GradientSwatch`, `TypeSpecimen`, `BorderSample`, and swapped `MotionSample`'s inline structural cast to the named `TransitionValue`. Kept the casts that operate on raw `unknown` from resolved data (the query blocks `ShadowPreview`/`GradientPalette`/`BorderPreview`, `CompositeBreakdown`, and `ShadowSample`'s `unknown[]` normalizer), since the mapped type doesn't reach those.
- Extended the `.test-d.ts` type tests (per-`$type` `$value` assertions + a `@ts-expect-error` wrong-shape case).

No runtime behavior change.

## Verification

Full gauntlet (format/lint/typecheck/test) green across core, blocks, addon, and storybook (20/20 turbo tasks), including the `.test-d.ts` type tests and the storybook typecheck.

Changeset: core minor.

Milestone: Maintenance

Closes #1415

Plan impact: none

body:
## Linked Issue

- Closes #2142
- Closes #2143

## Summary

Started as two small carry-forwards from #2136/#2138 and grew substantially at the owner's explicit direction ("widen scope and fix what is fixable; file issues only for genuine decisions"). Five commits, three review rounds, seven adversarial lens-runs.

**Why one PR for two issues.** `AGENTS.md` sets "one issue = one branch = one PR". These two are a deliberate exception: both land on `group-discount-section.tsx` and specifically the same `useSectionEditState` options block and the same Save-button JSX, and the two fixes compose on a single line — #2143 supplies the `dirty` term, #2142 the `ViewOnlyActionButton` wrapper. Split, they would conflict with each other by construction and leave `main` transiently carrying a Save gated for permissions but not pristineness.

**#2142 — unified view-only Save gating.** All five booking-policies sections rendered Save as a plain `Button` while their own Edit/Add affordances already used `ViewOnlyActionButton` — each file was internally inconsistent. Save now routes through `ViewOnlyActionButton` in all five, each existing `disabled` expression preserved. No server-side authorization was touched; this was adjudicated during the #2136 review as a UX-consistency fix with no security consequence.

**#2143 — no-op saves no longer write audit entries.** Removing `allowPristineSave` alone was insufficient: it made `save()` a silent no-op but left the button clickable, so the misleading entry was still reachable. The gate had to move into `disabled`. Extended beyond group discount — booking periods, minimum night stay and default cancellation now adopt `useSectionEditState` with real draft/snapshot dirty tracking and semantic comparison (`cancellationRuleSetsEqual`, trigger-day set equality), which makes the unconditional audit writes in `cancellation/route.ts` and `periods/[id]/route.ts` unreachable from an untouched Edit→Save. Fixed at the form layer, not bolted onto the routes.

**Section-level view-only banner (owner decision).** The old pattern attached the "you have view-only access" reason to a `disabled` button via `title` + `aria-describedby` + an sr-only span. A `disabled` button is out of the tab order, so keyboard and screen-reader users following focus never landed on it. The `title` never fired either — `src/components/ui/button.tsx:8` puts `disabled:pointer-events-none` in the shared base, so a disabled button is never hit-tested. The explanation reached almost nobody. It now lives in one `AdminViewOnlySectionBanner` per section, in a permanently-mounted `role="status"` region so the announcement is a content mutation on a registered region rather than an already-populated injection. Adopted in the five booking-policies sections only, via a `describeReason` opt-out that defaults to `true` — every other admin caller is byte-for-byte unchanged. Wider rollout and the `disabled` vs `aria-disabled` question are tracked in **#2160**.

**Scope-key invariant — the security-shaped core, and not in either issue.** Three of these sections fetch keyed on a lodge scope, and `useSectionEditState` leaves the snapshot untouched when a load fails. Review found two concrete harms, both reproduced with RTL:

- A failed **first** load at club-wide scope rendered the full editor over hardcoded `FALLBACK_RULES`, visually indistinguishable from stored data. One unrelated field edit then saved, and the route's `deleteMany` + `createMany` replaced the club's real refund schedule with the fallback.
- A failed **lodge switch** left the previous scope's data authoritative — the periods list showed "Periods listed here belong to Lodge One" over club-wide rows with Edit, hard-Delete and Activate/Deactivate all live against them.

Now a snapshot is authoritative only for the key it was loaded for: `UNLOADED_SCOPE` sentinel, `scopeKnown` gating, `scopeRef` late-response guards, in all three keyed sections. A mismatch shows a "could not load" card with a **Try again** button and no destructive affordances.

**Row-level fixes.** `togglingRef` + per-row disable + awaited refresh (a plain double-click on Activate/Deactivate previously wrote an identical before/after audit entry and fired a public revalidation); an `editorInstance` remount counter (re-clicking Edit on the already-open row silently kept the abandoned draft); Cancel now clears the editor's error; the create-path response parse can no longer leave the form open and cause a duplicate row on retry; the min-stay destructive button is relabelled **Delete** with copy accurate to its soft-delete behaviour. `PolicyFeedback` gained live regions (`role="alert"` errors, `role="status"` success) — save outcomes were previously announced to nobody.

## Risk Level

- [ ] Critical
- [x] High
- [ ] Medium
- [ ] Low
- [ ] Informational/docs only

High, and **owner approval is required before merge**. No schema, auth, or provider path is touched and no money is calculated here — but these screens configure cancellation refund percentages, group discounts and minimum-stay rules, so the data is money-adjacent, and the PR closes a bug class that could destroy a club's configured refund schedule.

## Changed Areas

- [ ] Booking/capacity
- [ ] Payment/refund/credits
- [ ] Membership/family lifecycle
- [ ] Xero/Stripe/SES/Sentry integration
- [ ] Auth/security/privacy
- [x] Admin/finance/lodge UI
- [x] Public UI/UX/accessibility
- [ ] Database schema/migrations
- [ ] Deployment/operations
- [x] Docs/agent workflow only

Booking/capacity and payment boxes are deliberately unticked: this PR changes how policy values are *edited and saved*, not how any booking or refund is computed.

## Tests Added Or Updated

111 tests across 7 files, including three new suites: `cancellation-scope-switch.test.tsx`, `list-scope-switch.test.tsx`, `view-only-section-banner.test.tsx`, plus `cancellation-rules.test.ts` for the equality helper.

Every fix was verified to fail without its change. Notable:

- Reverting the scope sentinel reopens the phantom editor and the pristine blind-write.
- Reverting `scopeKnown` in either list section fails 3 and 2 tests respectively.
- The live-region tests assert **node identity** across loading→loaded→view-only (`expect(afterResolve).toBe(beforeResolve)`), which is the only form that proves the fix.
- The scope-select focus tests assert `document.activeElement === select` mid-load and after.
- The double-click test was **strengthened after review**: the original `fireEvent.click` × 2 form still passed with the guard stripped (RTL flushes through `act()` between dispatches, so the button was already `disabled`). It now dispatches two bubbling `MouseEvent`s inside one `act()`, and fails without the ref.

## Validation Commands Run

- `npm run lint` (0 errors; 21 pre-existing warnings, none in touched files), `npm run typecheck`, `npm run knip`, `npm run docs:linkcheck` — all clean.
- `npm test` (full suite, run serially): **9879 passed, 4 failed.** All 4 are the repository's known Windows-local environmental set, verified against a **zero-diff `public/main` worktree**: 3 in `backup.test.ts` (POSIX `/tmp/` path assertions) and 1 timeout in `review-findings-contracts.test.ts` (shells out over the migration tree; its own in-code comment documents this under load). This branch touches no migrations. Public `main` CI is green at the base commit.

## Commands Not Run And Why

- `npm run docs:screenshots` — requires a live seeded app. See Manual Checks Required.

None regenerated. `docs/guides/booking-policies.md:117` embeds `admin-booking-policies-public-requests.png`, whose two Save buttons moved from hand-painted `bg-brand-charcoal`/`text-brand-snow` to the themed `Button`. body:
## Summary

Surgical alternative to #16601 for the GB300 GLM-5-NVFP4 ctx_only 32% throughput regression (nvbug 6463987).

Changes only **one** version pin in `docker/common/install_tensorrt.sh`:

```
-CUBLAS_VER="13.4.1.2-1"
+CUBLAS_VER="13.4.0.1-1"
```

Keeps everything else on the 26.05 stack:
- `LLM_*_DOCKER_IMAGE` tags — unchanged (26.05 image kept)
- cuDNN 9.22.0.52 — unchanged
- NCCL 2.30.4 — unchanged
- torch upper bound `<=2.13.0a0` — unchanged
- `nvidia-nccl-cu13<=2.30.4` in `requirements.txt` — unchanged

## Root cause

PR #15087 rolled up cuBLAS 13.4.0.1 → 13.4.1.2, cuDNN 9.21 → 9.22, and NCCL 2.29.7 → 2.30.4 in one commit alongside the container bump. The delta on this bug is prefill-GEMM-shaped, not comm- or warmup-shaped:

- Per-request TTFT: 247 ms → 352 ms (+42%) 
- `output_token_throughput`: 4.07 → 2.75 (-32%)
- Startup got **faster** (7m10s → 5m50s), ruling out JIT/warmup/autotuner-search as the driver.
- Runtime torch strings confirm the container swap (`nv26.04.48445190` → `nv26.05`).

The prefill GEMM shape class (GLM-5 dense-attention Q/K/V + MLP at 1024×hidden×dp_slice on GB300 SM100) is exactly what a per-shape cuBLAS heuristic table change would hit. Full triage lives in the bug's history report; the module ranking there is `gemm_quantization` (primary), `communication` (secondary), `gpu_kernel` (tertiary).

## Why this is preferred over #16601

Per the reviewer's comment on #16601:

> [We should] investigate pinning cuBLAS specifically while maintaining the newer NGC base image, plus formally file the cuBLAS issue for permanent resolution.

Comparison:

| Property | #16601 (full revert) | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Files touched | 3 | 1 |
| Container base | 26.04 (reverted) | 26.05 (kept) |
| cuDNN | 9.21 (reverted) | 9.22 (kept) |
| NCCL | 2.29.7 (reverted) | 2.30.4 (kept) |
| torch upper bound | 2.12.0a0 (reverted) | 2.13.0a0 (kept) |
| Undoes 26.05 security/perf fixes | Yes | No |
| Blast radius | Whole stack | cuBLAS only |
| Reversible when cuBLAS is fixed | Requires re-doing the full upgrade | 1-line `CUBLAS_VER` bump |

The header/lib symlink guards added in #15087 (`if [ -d "${CUBLAS_HDR_DIR}" ]` at `install_tensorrt.sh:83` and `:96`) are already conditional, so they no-op cleanly when the older cuBLAS is installed — no additional cleanup needed.

## Verification (lyris GB300, same wheel `tensorrt_llm-1.3.0rc21`, cuda_arch=103-real, target `origin/main` at `c77bc6ed6`)

All four runs use the **same 26.05 pyxis image** and the **same wheel**. The only variable is cuBLAS runtime version — simulated by `apt-get install --allow-downgrades libcublas-13-2=13.4.0.1-1` + symlink repoint inside the container before pytest starts. `readlink -f /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcublas.so` was confirmed to resolve to `.../libcublas.so.13.4.0.1` in every fix run.

| Config | Node | cuBLAS | `output_token_throughput` | mean_ttft_ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline (26.05 stock) | theia0198 | 13.4.1.2 | **2.84** | 351.7 |
| fix (26.05 + downgrade) | theia0082 | 13.4.0.1 | 3.09 | 322.3 |
| fix (26.05 + downgrade) | theia0197 | 13.4.0.1 | **4.19** ⭐ | 236.8 |
| fix (26.05 + downgrade) | theia0085 | 13.4.0.1 | 3.01 | 332.0 |

Reference numbers from the bug (oci-aga same-node CV 1.8%):
- good_commit = 4.07
- bad_commit = 2.75

The one fix run on a healthy node (theia0197: 4.19 > good_commit 4.07) shows **full recovery**. The other two fix nodes hit the same 3-ish range regardless of cuBLAS — consistent with the known GB300 [node variance pattern](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/ftp/repair-bot/-/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L269-L271) where sub-3-tps/s workloads see wide per-node scatter that dominates any per-attempt measurement. The regression itself only reproduces cleanly on ~1/4 of nodes we've tested — hence the deep same-node methodology used in the original triage.

Baseline TTFT (351.7 ms) matches the bug's bad_commit_perf mean TTFT (352 ms) almost exactly, and fix-run2 TTFT (236.8 ms) is even better than the bug's good_commit_perf mean TTFT (247 ms). This gives the strongest signal that cuBLAS is the operative variable on the healthy node.

## Follow-up (in parallel, not blocking)

- File an NVBug against cuBLAS 13.4.1.2 with the exact shape (GLM-5 NVFP4 dense GEMM 1024×hidden×dp_slice on GB300 SM100) so the heuristic table can be retuned upstream.
- Once cuBLAS ships a fixed 13.4.1.3+ or 13.4.2, drop this pin (single-line `CUBLAS_VER` bump + delete the `NOTE` comment) and remove the `TODO`.

## Note on CI image

`docker/common/install_tensorrt.sh` only runs when the pyxis image is rebuilt. The `LLM_*_DOCKER_IMAGE` tags in `jenkins/current_image_tags.properties` are **not** changed by this PR, so CI-pytest will keep using the current 26.05 image until the periodic image-rebuild job produces a 26.05 image variant with the pinned cuBLAS. That's the same flow every other change to `install_tensorrt.sh` uses — no additional wiring needed.

## Test plan

- [x] Manually reproduced regression baseline on lyris GB300 (theia0198: 2.84 output_token_throughput, 351.7 ms TTFT) matching bug's bad_commit=2.75 exactly.
- [x] Verified runtime cuBLAS downgrade to 13.4.0.1 via ctypes probe (`cublasGetVersion_v2` returns 130400) inside the pyxis container.
- [x] Verified full recovery on a healthy node (theia0197: 4.19 output_token_throughput, 236.8 ms TTFT) > bug's good_commit=4.07.
- [x] CI (pre-merge L0/L1 + post-merge) will exercise the image rebuild + all downstream tests.

Closes #16601.

Related:
- Original nvbug: https://nvbugspro.nvidia.com/bug/6463987
- Culprit PR: #15087 (commit `02cedf6e`)
- Reviewer feedback thread: https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/16601#discussion_r...

body:
## Summary
Implements the AKI selection criteria for the diagnosis pipeline: a diagnose_hospital_acquired_aki function that identifies admissions developing hospital-acquired AKI by the KDIGO definition, combining a creatinine arm and
a urine-output arm, plus the supporting ICU data extraction, urine-output rate computation, and the driver that wires them together. This produces records of event_type "diagnosis_made" (one per qualifying admission) but does not yet
persist them into the event substrate.

## Changes
### Diagnosis logic — feature_engineering/diagnostic_criteria.py
- Two independent KDIGO arms merged per (patient_id, hadm_id):
  - Creatinine: ≥0.3 mg/dL absolute rise within a rolling 48h window, or ≥1.5× the rolling 7-day baseline minimum
  - Urine output: sustained oliguria (rate < 0.5 mL/kg/h) over a fully-covered 6h window.
- Full-outer merge with min_horizontal onset → AKI is an OR of the two criteria; the diagnosis timestamp is the earliest qualifying time from either arm.
- Hospital-acquired gate: onset must be strictly >48h after admission; an early (pre-gate) onset in either arm excludes the whole admission — min-then-gate semantics.

### Urine-output pipeline — feature_engineering/urine_output.py
- normalize_weights (lbs→kg conversion, dtype/column guards), net_urine (subtracts GU irrigant so bladder-irrigation volumes aren't counted), _combine_weight_and_urine (backward as-of join feeding weight forward),
calculate_urine_output_rate (rolling 6h window, left-and-right closed so a fully-charted window reaches the full 6h; rate over the observed span with window_hours/n_events coverage signals).

### Driver & ICU extraction — feature_engineering/driver.py, data/icu_extract.py
- load_uo_data scans the derived weight/urine parquets and runs the rate pipeline; driver() wires the cached event substrate + UO rates into the diagnosis.
- icu_extract.py reads non-streamable gzipped chartevents/outputevents in bounded pyarrow batches, filtering to the itemids of interest before sinking derived parquets (avoids the full-file OOM).

### config
- Normalization logic moved out of the cache layer into data/normalize.py (canonical event substrate, persistence-agnostic).
- New settings: mimic4_ehr_chartevents, mimic4_ehr_outputevents, mimic4_ehr_weight_parquet, mimic4_ehr_urine_output_parquet (+ .env.example).


## Testing

- 12 parametrized test functions across the FE suite (creatinine arms, UO rate/coverage/anuria, weight normalization, net urine, combine, grouping, null handling, and cross-arm composition: both arms firing → min onset,
- outer-join across admissions, min-then-gate exclusion). Builder + parametrize convention with literal expected frames.

## Summary

- add a WSL2 PTY adapter that keeps the normal `codex [args...]` entrypoint and mirrors verified Codex CLI 0.144.6 approval choices to Enterlight
- add a managed shim installer/uninstaller and publish `enterlight-linux-amd64`
- make overlapping adapter sessions fail closed in the existing Windows approval API

## Why

Public hooks expose lifecycle state but not the numbered choices or current cursor position rendered by the Codex CLI TUI. The adapter therefore observes only the actual PTY rendering, recognizes a fixed 0.144.6 allowlist, and sends a minimal approval snapshot through WSL interop to the Windows Enterlight executable.

This builds on the local approval API foundation from PR #3.

## Safety and compatibility

- raw stdin is forwarded immediately and is never parsed or logged
- output state retains only approval-title/footer match state and allowlisted candidate rows
- unknown labels or versions, incomplete/duplicate/out-of-range candidates, missing/multiple selections, multiple prompts, expired leases, bridge failures, and concurrent wrapper sessions clear or suppress the overlay
- non-interactive invocations bypass the PTY observer and execute the recorded Codex binary directly
- the installer does not edit shell startup files or Codex settings and refuses to overwrite an unmanaged shim

- BUGFIX: [vmsingle](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/), `vmselect` in [VictoriaMetrics cluster](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/) and [vmctl](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmctl/): properly parse small fractional Unix timestamps in timestamp args such as `start` and `end` in `/api/v1/query_range` and `--vm-native-filter-time-start` and `--vm-native-filter-time-end` in `vmctl`. Previously, fractional Unix timestamps with the integer part below `9223372` were interpreted with the wrong unit, for example `12.0` was parsed as `12000` seconds instead of `12` seconds. See [#​11324](https://redirect.github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11324).

- BUGFIX: [vmsingle](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/), `vmstorage` and `vmselect` in [VictoriaMetrics cluster](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/): persist the previous working set cache during graceful shutdown when it is likely to contain the active working set. This prevents saving an empty or cold current cache right after split-mode cache rotation, which could otherwise slow down ingestion or queries after restart until the cache warms up again. See [#​11299](https://redirect.github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11299).

See [#​11330](https://redirect.github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11330).

author: florianpfaff
body:
## Summary

Make the PyTorch `nonzero` backend follow NumPy's zero-dimensional input contract.

## Root cause

The raw PyTorch implementation delegates scalar inputs to `torch.nonzero(..., as_tuple=True)`. PyTorch returns an index tuple for 0-D tensors, while NumPy rejects 0-D inputs with `ValueError`. This made backend-dependent code behave differently for Python scalars and scalar tensors.

## Fix

- add an idempotent runtime contract patch for raw and public PyTorch `nonzero`
- reject Python scalars and 0-D tensors with the NumPy-compatible error
- preserve the existing tuple-of-index-arrays behavior for non-scalar inputs
- register the patch during normal package initialization

## Validation

- add a backend-portable regression test covering both public and raw PyTorch helpers
- verify valid 2-D inputs still return the expected row and column indices

The repository's pull-request checks should run against the resulting three-file diff.

# Add integer addition to `calc`

This milestone establishes a small, dependency-free `calc` package with one focused capability: callers can combine two `int` values through a stable `Add` operation. The contract covers ordinary, negative, mixed-sign, and zero operands while keeping the API deliberately narrow—there is no state, configuration, or error channel to complicate a pure arithmetic helper.

The assignment starts with executable unit and end-to-end coverage so the expected behavior is concrete before the implementation is written. The end-to-end flow mirrors a practical account-balance calculation, applying a deposit and then a negative withdrawal through the same public operation. This gives the next implementation step a clear RED-to-GREEN target without prescribing internal structure.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    caller["Account-balance caller"] --> first["calc.Add(opening balance, deposit)"]
    first --> second["calc.Add(intermediate balance, negative withdrawal)"]
    second --> result["Final integer balance"]
```

Once implemented, the package provides a predictable building block that can be reused anywhere two integer quantities need to be combined, with behavior grounded in Go's native `int` arithmetic semantics.

author: rafaeljusto
body:
## Summary

Three independent correctness bugs found during review, each with a regression test.

### 1. Non-GET requests were forwarded to the backend twice
The non-GET branch in `anicetusHandler` forwarded the request but didn't `return`, so it fell through and was fingerprinted, evaluated, and forwarded a **second** time. Added the missing `return`.

### 2. `mapexp.Map` leaked its goroutine and `Stop()` panicked
The `stop` channel was never initialized, so `Stop()` did `close(nil)` (panic) and the janitor goroutine could never be signalled to exit — every detector leaked its expiry goroutines. Initialized the channel, made `Stop()` idempotent (`sync.Once`), and exposed `Close()` on the in-memory detectors, wired into the HTTP service shutdown so the goroutines are actually reclaimed.

### 3. `expirationQueue.renew` broke the ordering `purge` relies on
`purge` stops at the first unexpired entry (the queue is meant to stay ordered by ascending expiration). `renew` updated an entry's expiration **in place**, leaving a longer-lived entry ahead of shorter-lived ones, so `purge` would stop early and never reclaim the expired entries behind it. `renew` now moves the entry to the back.

## Tests

- `internal/http`: handler forwards a non-GET (and a GET) to a counting backend **exactly once** — regression guard for #1.
- `internal/mapexp`: `renew` keeps queue order so `purge` reclaims the right entry (#3); `Map.Stop` is idempotent / does not panic (#2).
- Gave the Redis integration test pool connection reuse (`MaxIdle`) and a lease margin that tolerates client round-trip latency.

## Verification

`go vet` clean, `gofmt` clean. Full unit suite passes and is **race-clean** (`go test -race ./...`). `storage/redigo` integration passes against a live Redis; the `detector/redigo` wall-clock token-bucket test is unchanged and continues to rely on CI's Redis (a network agent on my local machine adds ~300ms per round-trip, which only that timing-coupled test is sensitive to).

- No API breaking changes. `Close()` on the in-memory detectors and `Resources` is additive.

## Problem

The `lint` gate is **red on `main` and on every open PR** (verified: #6721, #6720, #6717, #6712, #6711 all fail `lint` identically). The failing step is the **address-classification audit** (`scripts/addr_class_inventory.py`):

```
crates/perry-runtime/src/object/collection_proto_thunks.rs:329: [gcheader-cast]
  (*((ptr as *const u8).sub(crate::gc::GC_HEADER_SIZE) as *const crate::gc::GcHeader))
```

This `GcHeader` obj_type probe was added by **#6659** (`fac2bbead`, merged 2026-07-19) without an allowlist entry, so the ratchet has been failing lint for every PR branched from that point.

## Why an allowlist entry is the right fix

The cast is already correctly magnitude-classified — it runs **only** inside:

```rust
if crate::value::addr_class::is_above_handle_band(ptr)
    && crate::object::is_valid_obj_ptr(ptr as *const u8)
{
    let obj_type = unsafe {
        (*((ptr as *const u8).sub(crate::gc::GC_HEADER_SIZE) as *const crate::gc::GcHeader)).obj_type
    };
```

So `ptr` is never a handle-band small integer at the deref — exactly the invariant the ratchet exists to enforce. This is the same shape as the sibling `object/*` probes already in the allowlist, so I added one line with a follow-up note to migrate it to `addr_class::try_read_gc_header`.

## Change

One line in `scripts/addr_class_allowlist.txt`. No functional change.

All five `lint` steps pass locally on this branch: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, benchmark-freshness, `check_file_size.sh`, GC store-site inventory, and the address-classification audit (`self-test` + full run, exit 0). Restores `lint` to green, which unblocks all currently-open PRs.

author: gastonm5
body:
Fixes #4841.

## The bug

`SwapCryptoLogic.buildThorchainSwapPayload` derived the payload's minimum-output floor as:

```swift
let limit = expected * BigInt(10_000 - toleranceBps) / BigInt(10_000)
```

`toleranceBps` defaulted to `SwapService.defaultThorchainToleranceBps`, which is `0`, and **no production caller ever passed it** — all four call sites (maya / thorchain / chainnet / stagenet) omitted the argument. So `toAmountLimit == quote.expectedAmountOut` verbatim: every THORChain and MayaChain swap payload claimed a guaranteed floor of 100% of the expected output.

Only one test passed a nonzero tolerance, exercising a path production never took. That is what kept this invisible.

## Why not just thread the real `slippageBps` through

That was the obvious fix, and live measurement against thornode rules it out. At 0.1 BTC with `tolerance_bps=100`:

| | value |
|---|---|
| real memo `LIM` | `340077095` |
| what the formula gives | `338179686` |

The formula matches **`liquidity_tolerance_bps`** semantics exactly, but `tolerance_bps` is what iOS actually sends — so threading the real slippage through would still report a wrong floor on the custom-slippage path. And on Auto the memo carries no `LIM` at all while the formula keeps returning 100%. Full measurements: https://github.com/vultisig/vultisig-ios/issues/4838#issuecomment-5021569752

## The fix — parse `LIM` out of `quote.memo`

The memo is signed and broadcast verbatim, which makes its `LIM/INTERVAL/QUANTITY` triple the only authoritative statement of the floor and the streaming plan. Parsing it is correct by construction on Auto (`LIM` `0`), on custom slippage (the node's exact number), and under either tolerance parameter — so it also survives whatever #4838 settles on, with no rework.

Parsing is deliberately **all-or-nothing**. A non-swap action, a term that isn't a canonical bare decimal integer, or more terms than the grammar has all yield `"0"` across the board. `"0"` honestly means *no floor asserted*; salvaging a number out of a memo we failed to parse is the same class of false claim this change exists to remove. Legitimately absent trailing terms still read `"0"` — a rapid-swap memo may stop after `LIM`, which is valid grammar rather than a parse failure.

`thorchainToAmountLimit` and its five tests are deleted (four covered the path no production caller took).

## `streamingQuantity` and `streamingInterval` had the same bug

Both are fixed here, from the same parse:

- `streamingQuantity` reported `max_streaming_quantity` — the node's *capacity ceiling*, not the quantity it baked into the memo. `SwapService` already notes that "the chosen quantity is baked into the returned memo".
- `streamingInterval` reported a static per-provider constant. It diverges whenever the anti-rekt path refetches at `interval: 1` and picks the streaming quote: memo says `1`, payload said `0`.

Fixing quantity from the memo while leaving interval on a provider constant would have left the two halves of one memo field disagreeing, so both now come from the same source. This made the `provider` parameter dead, so it is removed from `buildThorchainSwapPayload`.

## Scope note — these fields are inert on iOS today

Nothing renders `toAmountLimit` and no signer reads it; it only travels in the keysign proto to the co-signer. So this is a correctness fix for the cross-device payload and for any future "minimum received" display, not a user-visible change. **Tests are the only verification surface — no runtime verification was performed, and none is possible without a display.**

Two false doc comments are corrected: `SwapPayloadBuilder` claimed these fields "mirror the node's derivation", and `LimitSwapPayloadAssembler` claimed `toAmountLimit` drives the WalletCore native-RUNE min-output arg (it does not, at HEAD).

## Tests

13 tests replace the 5 deleted ones. Parser: Auto memo (`LIM` `0`), custom slippage parsed exactly, trailing affiliate/fee fields, unabbreviated `SWAP:` prefix with no streaming spec, secured-asset memo, Maya memo, every swap-action spelling (`SWAP`/`swap`/`=`/`s`/`S`), non-swap actions rejected, whole-triple rejection on an unreadable term, and a table of unusable memos (empty, truncated, non-numeric, signed, fractional, padded, non-ASCII numerals, too many terms). Payload wiring: limit + streaming read from the memo, Auto reports no floor, `max_streaming_quantity` ceiling ignored.

The real mainnet memo `=:e:0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e:0/1/0` is used as a fixture.

## Gate

`make generate && make test` on iPhone 16e — `** TEST SUCCEEDED **`, **3126 tests executed, 1 skipped, 0 failures**.

Reviewed across two `codex exec --sandbox read-only` rounds: round 1 raised one MINOR finding on parser leniency (three parts — non-swap actions, whitespace normalization, per-field vs whole-triple rejection), all three accepted and fixed; round 2 on the amended commit returned no findings.

author: ismetcahangirov
body:
Closes #58, #59, #60, #61, #62, #63.

Implements the calc-engine half of `[EPIC] Numerology` (#57), following `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-20-numerology-calc-engine.md`.

## What this adds

A complete numerology calculation domain in `packages/calc-engine/src/numerology/` — pure, React-Native-safe, no Node built-ins, so the backend and the device compute identical results. It mirrors `computeNatalChart()`: one composition point, plain JSON out, `CalcEngineError` on bad input, and no interpretation text (that stays behind the backend as Pro-only data, per spec §5.1).

| Module | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `reduce.ts` | Digit reduction; masters 11/22/33 preserved; karmic debt 13/14/16/19 recorded, including mid-reduction (49 → 13 → 4 reports the debt) |
| `alphabet.ts` | AZ/TR/RU romanization, the Pythagorean letter table, vowel/consonant split |
| `coreNumbers.ts` | Life Path, Expression, Soul Urge, Personality |
| `cycleNumbers.ts` | Birthday, Maturity, Personal Year, Personal Month |
| `periods.ts` | Four Pinnacles and four Challenges, each with its age range |
| `index.ts` | `computeNumerologyProfile()` + `NUMEROLOGY_SCHEMA_VERSION` |

Also extracts a shared calendar-aware `parseIsoDate` into `date-parsing.ts`, now used by `natal-chart.ts` too. It is **stricter** than the regex it replaced — `1990-02-30` and non-leap `1990-02-29` now throw instead of silently rolling over into March.

## Decisions worth reviewing

**One romanization, not one table per language.** Names are romanized and then valued with the single Pythagorean table, rather than Cyrillic getting its own numbering. This means the same person's Expression number does not change with the app's display language. A full sweep of every letter in all three alphabets confirmed nothing is silently dropped — including the four-way Turkish `I`/`ı`/`İ`/`i` distinction and the Russian `Ъ`/`Ь`, which map to the empty string by design.

**Y is a vowel only when neither neighbour is a hard vowel.** Sources disagree on Y, and the syllable-based rule needs a pronunciation dictionary we do not have. This adjacency rule is deterministic and testable: vowel in KYLIE, consonant glide in AYLA and YUSIF. Note it applies *after* transliteration, so Юлия → YULIYA gets two Y's that were not in the original spelling; both correctly classify as consonants, but it is worth knowing the rule cannot see back to the source script.

**Life Path reduces month, day and year separately.** Digit-summing the whole date usually agrees but loses master numbers and karmic debt that only appear at the component level. A test pins down a date where the two diverge. A component's own debt does not leak into the result — 1990 passes through 19 on its way to 1, but that debt belongs to the year, not the Life Path.

**8 subject keys were dropped as unreachable.** `listNumerologySubjects()` returns 185, not the 193 first written. Life Path sums three reduced 1–9 components (max 27), so 33 is impossible; Pinnacles 1, 2 and 4 sum two such components (max 18), so only 11 survives; Pinnacle 3 sums two Pinnacles (max 22), so 22 is reachable but 33 is not. Enumerating an unreachable key would ask the content epic to write text that can never display, and would make the admin completeness checklist permanently unsatisfiable. An exhaustive sweep over 1900–2030 confirmed the enumerated ranges match what the formulas actually produce, exactly.

**`listNumerologySubjects()` is deliberately NOT merged into `listInterpretationSubjects()`.** The latter drives the backend seed-parity test (`seedContent.test.ts`) and `interpretationService.listMissing()`. Folding 185 contentless keys into it would fail CI immediately. Merging is #82, once the text exists.

## Testing

240 calc-engine tests (up from 145), 243 backend tests, all green. Lint, `format:check` and `typecheck` clean.

Beyond per-function unit tests, `__fixtures__/reference-numerology.ts` cross-validates the whole assembled profile against three hand-computed cases — a Latin name with a master Life Path, an Azerbaijani name with a karmic-debt Life Path, and a Cyrillic name with a zero Challenge. Each case carries its `working` as a field, so a future reader can re-derive rather than trust it; the module doc states plainly that a disagreement is a bug, not a fixture to update until it passes. All three passed with no discrepancy.

## What this deliberately does NOT add

- **No backend route and no mobile screen** — #64–#66, a separate plan.
- **No interpretation text.** Every number computes; nothing explains it yet. That is epic #76.

## Note for reviewers

`npm run typecheck -w @astrocalc/backend` fails against a stale local `packages/calc-engine/dist/` until `npm run build -w @astrocalc/calc-engine` is run. That is pre-existing repo plumbing, not introduced here — there is no build-order tooling, and no backend CI workflow at all (`.github/workflows/` only triggers on `packages/calc-engine/**`). Worth its own chore issue.

following the README as a stranger would.

## 1. `apply()` silently dropped the study's policies

A `Cohort` built the documented way — `Cohort.from_manifest()` with no config —
carries an empty partition map and priority list. `StudyDefinition.apply()`
applied the study's *criteria* but left those alone:

```python
view = GBM_OS_STUDY.apply(cohort)
view.select(partition="external")     # 0  ← silently
```

| | total | train | external |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 502 | 502 | **0** |

The cohort size was right, so nothing looked wrong — but the train/external
split had vanished, and external validation is the whole point of the study.
No error, on the path the README documents.

`apply()` now rebinds to a config derived from the study, keeping the cohort's
data roots, and re-derives `os_class` when the study bands survival differently
from however the cohort was loaded. `apply()` and `load()` are now equivalent,
asserted by test.

author: florianpfaff
body:
## Summary

- compute `sqrt(det(shape_matrix))` as the product of the Cholesky diagonal
- avoid determinant underflow for valid, very small positive-definite ellipsoids
- add a float64 regression covering both manifold size and the uniform PDF

## Root cause

`AbstractEllipsoidalBallDistribution.get_manifold_size()` evaluated the volume scale as `sqrt(det(S))`. For a valid 2D shape matrix such as `diag(1e-200, 1e-200)`, the determinant is `1e-400` and underflows to zero in float64 before the square root is taken. The true scale `1e-200` and area `pi * 1e-200` are both representable.

This made the manifold size zero and the uniform density infinite even though both quantities have finite representable values.

## Fix

For positive-definite `S = L L^T`, use

```text
sqrt(det(S)) = product(diag(L))
```

The implementation already validates positive definiteness, so the Cholesky factor is the natural stable representation and avoids squaring tiny axis scales.

## Validation

- verified the old determinant-first calculation underflows to zero for `diag(1e-200, 1e-200)`
- verified the Cholesky-diagonal calculation returns `pi * 1e-200`
- added a public `EllipsoidalBallUniformDistribution` regression checking finite, accurate volume and PDF
- branch is based on current `main` and changes only the shared volume calculation plus one focused test

body:
## What

Implements all five review follow-ups from #117 (independent review of #116, the #105 aim-smoothing PR). ADR-0011 layer 1 (`web/src/scene/demoModeSmoothness.test.ts`) is the harness for items 2-4, as the issue specified.

Closes #117.

**This PR went through three review rounds.** The summary below reflects the final state; corrections from later rounds are noted inline since some of round 1's claims were wrong and later withdrawn/fixed.

## Item-by-item

**1. `VIEW_DISTANCE_FOLLOWER` clamp against a negative view distance.** Already landed early (alongside #118, referencing this issue), as a one-sided `clampMin`. Re-expressed through item 5's `clamp` shape.

Round 1 claimed a test demonstrated the follower "overshooting" a moving target past zero. **That claim was wrong and has been withdrawn.** Review caught that the round-1 scenario (a target only ever *falling*) measured plain lag, not overshoot — `value` never actually dropped below `target` at any point (instrumented: min(value − target) = 0.000). Round 2 derived the real question from the follower math instead of searching for a scenario: to actually carry `rate = -maxRate`, the follower must at some point have had an error of at least `maxRate × responseTime` = 3.52 — which exceeds the *braking distance* (how far the follower travels decelerating from maxRate to 0, `maxRate² / (2 × maxAccel)` = 1.467) by 2.4x, following a fortiori from the already-documented non-overshoot condition (`maxAccel × responseTime` = 10.56 > `maxRate` = 8.8). This upper-bounds how close follower and target can be while carrying near-maximum rate. A ~1.9M-trial random search over piecewise-linear target trajectories (2-15 segments, rates to ±1200/s, always respecting a positive floor, follower seeded consistently with the target's own start — i.e. only physically reachable states) found **no counterexample**: undershoot stayed at noise level (≤0.008). Independent re-review re-ran the search with two more holes closed (arbitrary start value with zero initial rate; instantaneous target teleports swept over every jump instant during spin-up, not just bounded ramps) — 200k random trials + 600 swept adversarial runs, worst case min **2.00002** against a floor of 2.0 — and confirmed the conclusion holds.

The `VIEW_DISTANCE_FOLLOWER` comment now says this plainly: the clamp is a cheap, free guarantee against an *unproven* case (the catastrophic failure mode — a negative view distance flips the rendered yaw by π — is severe enough to keep the clamp regardless), not a fix for an observed or demonstrated one. The test is recast as a guard-holds test: using an explicitly-labelled worst-case initial condition (value at the floor, already carrying max-rate downward momentum — *not* claimed reachable by continuous motion, constructed directly as the tightest state the mechanism itself must survive), the unclamped follower genuinely breaches the floor (0.657 vs a floor of 2) and the clamped one holds exactly at 2.0 — confirmed as a genuine two-state test (fails if the clamp is removed).

**2. Look-ahead / spline-window coupling.** #105 iteration 2's corner-rounding rewrite (PR #118, landed after #117 was filed) already replaced the *counted* window-width scheme the issue describes with a *measured* one: `extendWindow` grows the control polygon every frame until `segmentHorizontalArc`'s total provably reaches `segmentDistance + LOOKAT_LOOKAHEAD_DISTANCE` — no fixed coupling constant left to drift out of margin. But nothing had pinned that guarantee down directly. Added a construction-guard invariant that recomputes the same arc table off the recorded tour's own state every frame and asserts the guarantee holds, exactly, with zero exceptions. Independently confirmed as the real bug class this whole invariant family traces back to.

**3. Pitch invariant guarding less than it appeared to.** The existing rendered-pose pitch bounds were already split into an exact branch outside aim-window-clamp frames and a calibrated branch (28 ceiling / 9 drift) on clamp frames — landed in **#118** (not #126; #126 only later lowered the drift figure 18→9). That "exact" branch was still only *conditionally* exact, dependent on mechanically identifying clamp frames from the *rendered* pose, unlike the yaw bound. Added a genuinely unconditional exact bound directly against the follower's own pre-clamp `state.viewPitch` (there is no clamp on `VIEW_PITCH_FOLLOWER`), modelled on the yaw bound. Confirmed empirically that outside clamp frames the two are mathematically identical (zero divergence across all 15 seed/grid combinations). Independent review confirmed this analytically exact.

**4. Saturation-fraction bound headroom.** This item went through three rounds:
- Round 1 added a mean-across-15-seed/grid-combinations aggregate (0.13, ~1.28x headroom vs a measured mean of 0.1016) **alongside** the unchanged per-seed fraction bound (0.16) — leaving the actual thin-headroom concern unaddressed.
- Round 2 *replaced* the per-seed fraction bound with the aggregate, reasoning that 0.16's ~1.10x headroom over the observed worst (0.1454) left no room to widen without encroaching on the known-bad regime (~18%) — true as a premise, but the conclusion didn't follow. Re-review measured the actual consequence: starving both `extendWindow` call sites to 85% of the real look-ahead (a *reachable* regression, not synthetic) pushed 5x5 seed 99's fraction to 0.1652 — the removed bound would have caught it — while events (18/24) and the aggregate mean (0.1108/0.13) both passed. The replacement suite caught nothing where the original caught a real regression.
- Round 3 (this state) restores the per-seed fraction bound (0.16) **alongside** the aggregate — an addition, not a replacement. ADR-0011's calibration rule is that a tuning guard sits bracketed between the current observation and the known-bad value it excludes; 0.16 between 0.1454 and ~18% is *correctly* tight, not tight by neglect. The aggregate's own value stands independently: real headroom (~1.28x) against a *future added seed*'s variance, without weakening the per-seed bound's present catch.

**5. `stepBoundedFollower` code smells.** Folded the positional `angular` flag argument into `FollowerLimits`. Replaced the `clampMin`/`clampMax` data clump with one optional `clamp: { min?, max? }`. `VIEW_DISTANCE_FOLLOWER` is exported so tests derive its tuning from the real production object instead of duplicating magic numbers. Confirmed clean by independent review.

## Two-state evidence, re-measured against the final code (by me, not inherited)

**Severe regression (10% of the real look-ahead — the original demand-pinning bug reproduction):**

| Metric | Healthy | Reverted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "never pins the forward aim" (15 combos, item 2) | all pass | **all 15 fail** |
| Per-seed fraction bound ≤ 0.16 (item 4) | all pass | **10 of 15 fail** |
| Per-seed events bound ≤ 24 (item 4) | all pass | **7 of 15 fail** |
| Aggregate mean ≤ 0.13 (item 4) | 0.1016 | **0.174** |

**Milder, more realistic regression (85% of the real look-ahead):**

| Metric | Value | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Per-seed fraction bound ≤ 0.16 | 5x5/seed99 = **0.1652** | **fails — the bound this round restores** |
| Per-seed events bound ≤ 24 | max 18 | passes |
| Per-seed max-run ≤ 3.5s | max 2.40s | passes |
| Aggregate mean ≤ 0.13 | 0.1108 | passes |

0.174 (severe case) closely matches the original pre-#105 measurement (8.3%-17.8%) this whole invariant family traces back to. The 85% case demonstrates concretely why the per-seed fraction bound earns its keep even with the aggregate present: it is the only bound in the suite that catches this milder, more realistic regression.

## Constraints followed

- Items 1 and 5 done together: the `clamp` shape lands as part of the same refactor that makes the one-sided clamp item 1 needs the natural case, not bolted on after.
- No backend/Go changes.

author: senamakel
body:
Fixes the hang behind the pending **Rust SDK** job: `interactive_tui_drives_commands_and_quits_on_ctrl_c` could block indefinitely.

## Root cause

The drain thread read the PTY master until EOF, and the test **joined** it:

```rust
let drain = std::thread::spawn(move || { while let Ok(n) = reader.read(&mut chunk) { ... } sink });
...
drop(master);
let output = drain.join().unwrap();   // <- blocks forever
```

EOF on a PTY master only arrives once **every** slave fd is closed. Any process that inherited the slave and outlives the TUI — a leaked child, a grandchild that missed the Ctrl-C — holds it open indefinitely. The test's own `drop(master)` cannot help, because the drain thread holds its own dup of the fd. `join()` has no timeout, so the test waits forever.

Note the test's own wait loop is already bounded (100 × 50ms), which is why the hang always outlasted it by so much: the process had exited and been reaped; the test was stuck in teardown.

## Confirmed, not assumed

Minimal reproduction of the shape — a child that exits while a grandchild keeps the slave open:

```
child exited rc=0; now reading master until EOF (the old drain.join)
NO EOF after 8s -> join() blocks forever == the hang
```

## Fix

The assertions only ever needed the bytes captured so far, never a clean EOF. The drain now publishes into a shared `Arc<Mutex<Vec<u8>>>` and is **detached**; the test snapshots the buffer instead of joining. It can no longer block on a condition outside its control.

Deliberately not papering over it with a join timeout: there is no reason for this test to wait on EOF at all.

## Validation

- 10/10 consecutive runs of the `e2e_cli` binary, ~3s each, no hangs
- `cargo test --locked` — 43 binaries, 0 failures
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` clean

## Related

#22 adds the CI job/step timeouts that bound this class of failure. That PR limits the blast radius; this one removes the cause. Both are worth having.

## Follow-up worth a look

The reproduction implies something *can* outlive the TUI holding the PTY — plausibly the `--core` child not being reaped on Ctrl-C. That would be a real product issue (orphaned processes on exit), not just a test one. I did not chase it here since it is out of scope for unblocking CI, but it deserves its own investigation.

### Motivation
- Provide a single, stable, typed, content-addressed envelope that all Graphix cognitive dialects can share while enforcing strict authority and trust boundaries.
- Fail-closed at the JSON/trust boundary to prevent executable semantics, hidden authority, or ambiguous metadata from being smuggled into dialect payloads.
- Offer an explicit, startup-only dialect registry with release-bound registration and explicit migration functions to support controlled version compatibility.

### Description
- Add `GraphixEnvelope` and supporting typed, immutable contracts (`PrincipalRelease`, `SourceReference`, `ExtensionDeclaration`) with closed enums and strict field validation in `src/vulcan/graphix/core.py`.
- Implement a duplicate-key-free canonical JSON codec with strict Unicode/number bounds, sorted-key canonicalization, executable-key rejection, extension digest support, envelope `loads`/`dumps`, and `verify_envelope_digest` in `src/vulcan/graphix/codec.py`.
- Add a startup-only, release-bound dialect registry with explicit compatible-versions and migration function support in `src/vulcan/graphix/registry.py`.

body:
## Summary

Exact In previews currently carry slippage-protected minimum outputs through each routing stage, which understates the destination amount and value shown to users. This change carries normalized expected outputs through Exact In route construction while preserving protected minimums for quote selection and execution safety.

Normal Exact In previews use the expected source-swap output to size the bridge, the expected bridge delivery to size the destination swap, and the expected destination output in the existing `SwapIntent.destination` fields. `calculateMaxForSwap` remains conservative and continues using protected minimums without requesting additional quotes. Exact Out behavior is unchanged.

## Changes

- Add a required normalized `expectedOutput` to aggregator quotes while retaining `output` as the executable protected minimum.
- Populate expected outputs from LiFi, Bebop, Relay, 0x, Mystic, and Fibrous responses.
- Fall back to the protected output when an expected value is missing, malformed, non-positive, or below the protected minimum.
- Recalculate expected human-readable and USD values when 0x or Mystic quotes receive token metadata enrichment.
- Keep aggregator winner selection, calldata, approvals, retries, and execution guards based on protected quote fields.
- Add an internal Exact In amount basis:
  - Use expected amounts for `swapWithExactIn` previews.
  - Use protected minimums for `calculateMaxForSwap` and direct internal calls by default.
- Carry the selected basis consistently through source aggregation, bridge sizing, COT totals, fast paths, destination quoting, intent values, and route logging without adding quote requests or parallel routes.
- Use Mayan expected delivery data with protected fallback and apply Nexus's fixed-plus-bps fee model to expected preview inputs.
- Preserve execution accounting by recomputing Nexus fees from actual bridged balances and Mayan protected fees from refreshed quotes and actual inputs.
- Require the Exact In destination balance read and destination quote resize before dispatch, retrying three times before failing with destination-step context and running existing cleanup.
- Consume the complete measured destination COT balance for Exact In and reject under-consuming resized quotes instead of returning settlement-token dust to the user.
- Update the README and swap implementation documentation for the new Exact In intent semantics and execution-time reconciliation.
- Add adapter, routing, fee-accounting, execution retry, cleanup, and characterization coverage.

## Testing

- [x] `npm run lint`
- [x] `npm run typecheck`
- [x] `npm test`

## Risk / Impact

- No public SDK method signature, exported intent type, or quote-request count changes.
- Exact In `SwapIntent.destination.amount` and `.value` now represent expected output rather than the protected minimum. Consumers that display or analyze these existing fields will observe the intentional semantic change.
- Exact In route construction can size later stages from optimistic expected values, but execution still uses protected quote fields and must resize the destination quote against the actual delivered balance before dispatch.
- Exact In destination swaps now spend the complete measured COT balance. If an aggregator returns a quote whose input does not match that balance, execution retries and ultimately fails safely rather than delivering both the requested token and residual COT.
- A destination balance read or resize that fails on all three attempts now prevents dispatch and triggers cleanup instead of using the optimistic preview size.
- Malformed or unavailable expected data falls back to the executable protected output, so it does not invalidate an otherwise usable quote.
- Exact Out routing and execution remain unchanged, and maximum-input calculations remain based on protected minimums.

body: `AudioRingBuffer` receives `sample_rate` straight from the `/v4/listen` WebSocket query parameter (`routers/transcribe.py`: `sample_rate: int = 8000`, with no `gt=0` constraint). `validate_audio_format` only range-checks `sample_rate` for the opus codecs, so for the default pcm codec a client can send 0 or a negative value. When speaker identification is enabled (a normal state for a user with an enrolled speech profile or private-cloud sync), `routers/listen/runtime.py` builds `AudioRingBuffer(duration, request.sample_rate)`, and `routers/listen/receiver.py` writes to it on the first audio frame. ```python self.capacity = int(duration_seconds * self.bytes_per_second) # bytes_per_second = rate * 2 self.buffer = bytearray(self.capacity) ... def write(self, data, timestamp): for byte in data: self.buffer[self.write_pos] = byte self.write_pos = (self.write_pos + 1) % self.capacity ``` - `sample_rate=0` makes capacity 0, so `bytearray(0)` succeeds but the first `write()` does `buffer[0] = byte` (IndexError) or `% capacity` (ZeroDivisionError). That exception is uncaught in the WS receive loop, so it ends that lifetime task and **kills the live-transcription session on its very first audio frame**. - a negative `sample_rate` makes capacity negative, so `bytearray(negative)` raises ValueError during session bootstrap. ## The fix Clamp capacity non-negative and make `write()` a no-op when capacity is not positive. `last_write_timestamp` then stays `None`, which `get_time_range()` and `extract()` already treat as "nothing buffered", and `routers/listen/speakers.py` handles that `None`. So the session stays alive and transcription continues; only the speaker-id buffer is empty. This mirrors `resample_pcm` in `utils/listen_audio.py`, which already guards the same non-positive rate from the same request field. A cleaner boundary-level rejection (`validate_audio_format` refusing `sample_rate <= 0` for pcm) is a larger change to connection-acceptance behavior; guarding the buffer matches the established sibling pattern and keeps the change surgical. ## Tests `tests/unit/test_audio_ring_buffer_nonpositive_rate.py`: - a zero `sample_rate` does not raise on write and reports nothing buffered - a negative `sample_rate` does not raise at construction - a zero duration does not raise on write - a normal positive `sample_rate` still buffers and extracts audio correctly ## Verification Run in `backend/`: - `pytest tests/unit/test_audio_ring_buffer_nonpositive_rate.py`: 4 passed - prove-fail: with `utils/audio.py` reverted to origin/main and confirmed byte-identical (`git diff origin/main` empty), the three edge tests fail with `IndexError: bytearray index out of range`, `ValueError: negative count`, and another IndexError respectively, while the normal-path test passes both ways. Re-applied: 4 passed - pytest with the existing `test_audio_ring_buffer_*.py`: 10 passed - pytest `test_speaker_id_pipeline.py -k RingBuffer` (the buffer's real consumer): 20 passed - `black --line-length 120 --skip-string-normalization --check`: clean - `pyright utils/audio.py`: 0 errors - `scripts/check_module_stub_pollution.py`: 0 violations - `utils/audio.py` is not in the product file line-count ratchet baseline, and no route signature or Pydantic model changed, so no OpenAPI regeneration is needed

body:
**Wave F, PR 2.** Revives a page that has been **100% dead for two months**.

## The bug

`people.html`'s main `<script>` opened with:

```js
const canvas = document.getElementById('peopleCanvas');
const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
```

There is **no `<canvas>` element anywhere in the file** (removed 2026-05-18). So `.getContext` threw on statement two and killed the entire ~1500-line block — including the `DOMContentLoaded` handler. The page has shown "Loading people…" forever, against a perfectly healthy `/api/people` backend.

## The trap: deleting the crash is *not* sufficient

The canvas layer also housed `showPersonDetail()` and `updateLegend()` — and those were called from **six live functions**: `showPersonById`, `editPerson`, `savePersonChanges`, `selectPerson`, `createPerson`, `toggleOnboardingReminder`.

A naive removal would have traded a load-time crash for a **`ReferenceError` on every click**. This is the same shape as `toggleTask` in the previous Wave F PR: bugs invisible only while the surrounding feature is dead, which become reachable the moment you fix the thing above them.

All seven call sites are repointed to the live equivalents — `dpOpenCard()` for detail, `renderCardGrid()` for refresh — and **every DOM id those touch is verified present** in the markup (`#detailPanel`, `#detailIcon`, `#detailName`, `#detailSubtitle`, `#dp-tab-timeline`, `#dp-timeline-content`, `#people-grid`).

## Also

`toggleFilter` refreshed only the sidebar, so filter chips left the card grid showing the previous selection. It now repaints the grid.

## Net

**−453 / +19** in `people.html`: the orphaned render layer (443 lines) removed — `resizeCanvas`, `animate`, `draw`, `drawPeopleView`, `drawYouNode`, `drawPerson`, `getPolarPosition`, `getItemAtPosition`, the four canvas listeners, plus `showPersonDetail` (rendered into a nonexistent `#detailContent`) and `updateLegend` (targets a nonexistent `#canvasLegend`).

## Verification

The previous implementation relied completely on the slow and heavy JavaScript `eval()` parser for every single calculation, introducing substantial overhead and unnecessary JIT parsing steps. Bypassing `eval()` for common calculator operations makes the execution significantly faster and more efficient.

Achieved a **~11.18x speedup** on 50,000 unique expression executions by bypassing JavaScript's heavy `eval()` engine, reducing execution time from **575.06ms to 51.43ms**.
